old: The MYBA MOA is signed at heads of terms with a deposit (typically 10 percent), and closing follows 30 to 60 days later with payment of the balance, transfer of title, delivery, and a brief acceptance period (24 to 72 hours) during which the buyer can reject for material non-compliance with specification.
new: Under the MYBA Memorandum of Agreement (MOA), the buyer pays a deposit to a stakeholder on signing, commonly 10 percent, although the 2021 edition leaves the amount to be agreed. The sea trial and condition survey follow, and the buyer must give written notice of acceptance or rejection within the periods the MOA sets; after the sea trial the buyer can reject only for defects of the kind the form defines, and a buyer who gives no notice in time is treated as having accepted. Closing typically follows 30 to 60 days after signing, with payment of the balance, transfer of title and delivery at the same time. The deposit, the notice periods and the grounds for rejection are negotiated, so each should be read in the MOA actually signed.
reason: Acceptance under the MYBA MOA comes after survey and before completion, not after delivery; 2021 E-MOA deposit is agreed

old: Value-added tax (VAT) regime. The default is full VAT on purchase: 20 percent in France, 21 percent in Spain, 22 percent in Italy. On a EUR 4 million yacht the bill is EUR 800,000 to EUR 880,000.
new: Value-added tax (VAT) regime. Whether VAT is due on a purchase depends on where and how the yacht is supplied or imported, whether VAT has already been paid on it, and how it will be used. A yacht sold by a VAT-registered business in the EU, or imported into the EU for private use, attracts VAT at the standard rate of the country concerned, for example 20 percent in France, 21 percent in Spain and 22 percent in Italy; on a EUR 4 million yacht that is EUR 800,000 to EUR 880,000. A private sale of a yacht on which EU VAT has already been paid does not normally attract VAT again.
reason: Standard rates apply to taxable supplies and imports, not to every purchase
